chapter: Return to New York and the Embers
title: Answering the charge that Jonah went commercial
summary: He rejects claims that he went commercial; he enjoyed the songs like "On the Street Where You Live" and played them as well as he could.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: So, you know, like everything else, a lot of people, what you do, somebody's going to say something against it. So I had -- so a lot of guys say, "Oh, Jonah's gone commercial," when records started to hit and things like that, you know. But I don't look at it like that. I look at it like I enjoyed doing what I was doing. I don't think I limited myself in any way in the records that I played. You know, like those things, "On the Street Where You Live," and, "Baubles, Bangles and Beads." I played them the best I could play them. I didn't know them. The chords wasn't something that I did all the time, like, "Georgia Brown," and stuff. So I heard some guys. I just wanted to clear that up.
